t.3.36.1: Once, long ago, I too was roaming over this earth, proud in my valor, bearing the strength of a thousand elephants and resembling a mountain.
t.3.36.2: Resembling a dark rain-cloud, wearing earrings of refined gold, crowned and armed with an iron club, I roamed the Daṇḍaka forest, striking fear into the world and devouring the flesh of sages.
t.3.36.3: Then the righteous great sage Viśvāmitra, terrified of me, went in person to King Daśaratha and spoke these words to him.
t.3.36.4: Let this Rāma, ever vigilant, protect me at the time of the sacred rites, for a terrible fear has arisen in me because of Mārīca, O lord of men.
t.3.36.5: Thus addressed, the righteous-souled King Daśaratha then replied to the illustrious Viśvāmitra, the great sage.
t.3.36.6: This Rāghava is not yet sixteen years old and has not mastered the use of weapons. But whatever army is mine will gladly go with me, and I myself shall slay your enemy as you desire, O best of sages.
t.3.36.7: Thus addressed, the sage spoke again to the king: "Apart from Rāma, there is no other strength in the world sufficient against that rākṣasa."
t.3.36.8: Though only a boy, this one of great splendour is capable of subduing him. I shall go, taking Rāma with me; may it be well with you, O scorcher of foes.
t.3.36.9: Having spoken thus, the sage Viśvāmitra, supremely delighted, took the king's son with him and went to his own āśrama.
t.3.36.10: Then, in the Daṇḍaka forest, Rāma stood guard over him who had been consecrated for the sake of a sacrifice, drawing and twanging his wondrous bow.
t.3.36.12: Then Rāma was seen, illuminating the Daṇḍaka forest with his own blazing splendour, like the newly risen young moon.
t.3.36.11: He was a boy, his beard not yet grown, radiant and dark-complexioned, with auspicious eyes, wearing a single garment, bearing a bow, his hair in a topknot, and adorned with a golden garland.
t.3.36.13: Then I, resembling a cloud, wearing earrings of refined gold, mighty and endowed with a boon, came out of arrogance to his hermitage.
t.3.36.14: As I burst in all of a sudden with my weapon raised, I was seen by him; but on seeing me, he, unperturbed, strung his bow.
t.3.36.15: Out of delusion I scorned Rāghava, thinking, "This is a mere boy," and in great haste I rushed upon that sacrificial altar of Viśvāmitra.
t.3.36.16: Then he released a sharp arrow, destroyer of foes; struck by it, I was hurled into the ocean a hundred yojanas away.
t.3.36.17: Hurled away by the force of Rāma's arrow, my senses reeling, I was then cast down by him into the deep waters of the ocean. Regaining consciousness after a long while, dear one, I went to the city of Laṅkā.
t.3.36.19: Therefore, if you, though restrained by me, make war with Rāma, you will quickly meet with dreadful calamity and perish.
t.3.36.18: Thus was I then let go, while those companions of mine were struck down by Rāma, a mere boy not yet trained in weapons, yet tireless in his deeds.
t.3.36.20: You will bring torment and ruin upon the rākṣasas, who are versed in the ways of sport and pleasure and who delight in assemblies and festivals.
t.3.36.21: You will see the city of Laṅkā, crowded with mansions and palaces and adorned with many kinds of jewels, destroyed for the sake of Maithilī.
t.3.36.22: Even the pure, who commit no sins themselves, perish through the sins of others because they keep company with the wicked, just as fish perish in a lake inhabited by a serpent.
t.3.36.23: Through your fault you will see the Rākṣasas, their limbs smeared with divine sandalwood and adorned with divine ornaments, struck down upon the ground.
t.3.36.24: You will see the night-wanderers, those left over from the slain, some with their wives carried off and some still with their wives, helpless and without refuge, fleeing in the ten directions.
t.3.36.25: You will without doubt see Laṅkā covered by a net of arrows, enveloped in flames of fire, its mansions burnt down.
t.3.36.26: Thousands of lovely women are yours, O king, as your wives. Be devoted to your own wives and protect your own family, O Rākṣasa.
t.3.36.27: If you wish to enjoy for long your honor, your prosperity, your kingdom, and the life dear to you, do not do what is displeasing to Rāma.
t.3.36.28: Though strongly restrained by me, your friend, if you forcibly violate Sītā, you will go, your strength exhausted, together with your kinsmen, to the abode of Yama, your life taken by Rāma's arrows.
